solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Most apologetic as bishop, that is to say a good man

parts.note: as and so are interchangeable comparison words, as in 'as/so far as I know'
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is to say'
ST, saint, is the crossword's stock good man

explanation.surface: A contrite cleric is described as being as sorry as a bishop or a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Four short pieces in a row; 'that is to say' looks like a link phrase but supplies IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of sorry: the most regretful or contrite person is the sorriest.

clue.text: Worry being topless will make you different

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of the word is its first letter, which is lost

parts.note: to bother someone is to worry them

explanation.surface: Advice that dropping your anxieties will change you as a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: something other is something distinct or not the same.

clue.text: Directing is one trader's function

indicators.note: directing letters means steering them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says a trader's whole purpose is to direct things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directing' reads as the trader's job, but it signals the rearrangement of IS ONE TRADER.
explanation.definitionFit: A raison d'être (French, 'reason for being') is the purpose or role something exists to serve.

clue.text: Hospital department with decoration that's attractive

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
icing is the sugary decoration on a cake

explanation.surface: A hospital ward gets a makeover that makes it appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something tempting or alluring is attractive.

clue.text: For a bet, we both set off with the Parisian to climb tall building

indicators.note: set off suggests the letters are sent away to form something new
in a down clue, climbing reads the word upwards, so it is turned round

parts.note: le is French for 'the', as spoken in Paris

explanation.surface: Two people with a wager head off with a Frenchman to scale a skyscraper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' rearranges the wager words; 'to climb' works because this is a down clue, so the French article is read bottom to top. 'with' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Biblical tower at Babel was built to reach heaven, the archetypal tall building.

clue.text: Staunch guards on time had ambition

indicators.note: guards means the first word surrounds the second, as a guard encloses

parts.note: to staunch a flow is to dam it
re means 'on' or 'concerning'

explanation.surface: A loyal bodyguard on duty nursed bigger hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like the adjective 'loyal', but here it is the verb 'stop a flow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of dream in the sense of aspire: one who dreamt of success had that ambition.

clue.text: Oust awful despot, nearly last of type

indicators.note: awful describes the letters as being in a terrible state, so they are rearranged
nearly means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: the tyrant's word as written, shortened

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word type

explanation.surface: A call to overthrow a terrible tyrant, nearly the last of his kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims the tyrant's final letter before 'awful' shuffles what remains; 'last of type' reads like a description of the despot but supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to remove a ruler from power, to oust or dethrone them.

clue.text: Judgment from first person in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing signals that the spoken sound is what counts

parts.note: I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: A legal verdict delivered by the first witness at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court session but signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: having an eye for something means having discernment or good judgment about it.

clue.text: Is stomach convulsing? He might like it

indicators.note: convulsing describes the letters going into spasm and rearranging

explanation.surface: Asking whether a stomach cramp is happening, then suggesting someone might enjoy it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the pain of the convulsing stomach, which only one who enjoys suffering would like.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a person who takes pleasure in pain might like a stomach cramp.

clue.text: Economy? It's here in regularly chosen newspaper

indicators.note: regularly chosen means taking every second letter of the words

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, the newspaper hosting this puzzle

explanation.surface: A question about where savings are found, answered with the paper itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newspaper' is a nod to the Financial Times, where this puzzle appeared. 'regularly chosen' takes the even-placed letters of the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: frugality or careful management of money is economy.

clue.text: Rep's sorted somewhere to refuel, getting coffee

indicators.note: sorted means the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: Esso is a brand of petrol station, a place to fill a car's tank

explanation.surface: A sales rep, once settled at a petrol station, grabs a cup of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a strong Italian-style coffee made by forcing steam through grounds.

clue.text: Fabulous craft shop closed early

indicators.note: closed early means the word is cut off before its end

parts.note: Argos is a British catalogue store chain

explanation.surface: An amazing craft store shut its doors before the usual time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means 'of fable', not 'wonderful'; 'craft' is a vessel, not handiwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology: the ship sailed by Jason and his Argonauts in Greek legend, a vessel of fable.

clue.text: Irate banker becoming independent

parts.note: cross means angry or irate
bench and bank share a root (Italian banca, a money-changer's bench), so a bench is cheekily a banker

explanation.surface: An angry financier goes it alone.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Lords, crossbench peers sit apart from any party.
explanation.definitionFit: Political usage: crossbench members of Parliament or the Lords are unaligned with any party, so non-partisan.

clue.text: State retains influence for public roads

indicators.note: retains means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to state something is to express it
sway is power or influence over others

explanation.surface: The government keeps control over the highways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun (the government) but is the verb 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: high-speed highways, open to all traffic, are public roads.

clue.text: Form of artistic sport's difficult — can I cede?

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters are awkward and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A competitor finds an artistic sport hard and wonders whether to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a skating discipline judged on artistry, a kind of creative sport.

clue.text: Opening of curtains, the cue to upset sleeper

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: The curtains opening is the signal for a performer to be thrown off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeper' is not a person but a railway berth.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway usage: a couchette is a bunk on a night train, a sleeper berth.

clue.text: Worked steadily, almost achieving graceful movement

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it steadily

explanation.surface: A diligent dancer nearly masters an elegant move.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet: a bending of the knees with the back upright, a smooth dance motion.

clue.text: Poet X, curious name to take up

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: in a down clue taking up means reading the word upwards

parts.note: nosy means inquisitive or curious

explanation.surface: An unnamed poet is called X, an odd name to adopt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take up' reverses NOSY to YSON at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Discoloration of plant opening in spring within furrow

indicators.note: within means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a rut is a groove or furrow in the ground

indicators.note: the opening in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A garden blight appears as spring begins inside a ploughed furrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant pathology: a fungal disease giving orange-brown patches on leaves.

clue.text: Old gun with power, not second- rate performance

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: not tells you to remove the following letter

parts.note: Beretta is an Italian make of pistol
B is the second grade, as in B-movie

explanation.surface: A tired old weapon, with power but no second-class flaws, puts on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second-rate' looks like a description but is B, removed from BERETTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a light opera is a kind of staged musical performance.

clue.text: Old Mr Batty keeps one posh address

indicators.note: keeps means the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside
batty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An eccentric old gentleman keeps one grand home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' means a form of address, not a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Form of address: an old aristocratic way of speaking to a lord or nobleman.

clue.text: With contracted bill, whine EE's terrible mobile carrier

indicators.note: terrible shows the letters are in a mess and must be reordered
contracted means shortened by a letter

parts.note: the word bill as written, shortened

explanation.surface: A grumble about a phone contract bill from mobile operator EE.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' cuts BILL to BIL; 'terrible' rearranges BIL with WHINEEE. EE is a British mobile network; the answer is a wheeled rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: a wheeled rubbish bin carries waste and is movable, so a mobile carrier.

clue.text: Arm that's to shake if meeting the Queen

indicators.note: the answer, if it met the next piece, would make the word; so that piece is taken away

parts.note: to shiver is to shake or tremble
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A limb that trembles when introduced to royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' is a weapon, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a shiv is a makeshift knife, a weapon or arm.

clue.text: Family problem

definitions.meaning: a matter of concern or difficulty

explanation.surface: A household difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: legal word for children, and a point of trouble.

clue.text: Explosive article criminal mob hid in burial place

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: hid in means the rearranged letters are concealed inside

parts.note: a tomb is a grave or burial place

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A news story about a gang concealing loot in a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' shuffles the gang word and 'hid in' places the result inside the grave, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a nuclear fission weapon is an explosive device.

clue.text: Poor half-hearted workers

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its two middle letters; half of that heart is removed

parts.note: mean can mean poor or shabby, as in mean streets

explanation.surface: Badly paid employees lack enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: workforce staff are often called the men, as in management and men.

clue.text: Scattered leftover sandwiches beginning to sweat

indicators.note: sandwiches means it holds the next piece in the middle

parts.note: spare means surplus or left over

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Remnant sandwiches spread about start to sweat in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but is the verb 'enclose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: thinly spread or few and far between.

clue.text: Wanted money abroad sent back home

parts.note: the yen is the currency of Japan

indicators.note: sent back means the word is reversed

parts.note: a den is a lair or home

explanation.surface: Someone longed for cash from overseas to be posted home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns DEN into NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of yen, to long for: wanted or yearned.

clue.text: Officials from Nine Elms messed up

indicators.note: messed up means the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Match officials from Nine Elms, a district of south London, made blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: assistant referees who watch the touchlines are match officials.
